title: Antenatal and Postnatal Mental Health Screening

evidenceAudit.scope: Pregnant or postnatal woman: asking about mental health history at the booking visit, case-finding questions for depression and anxiety, validated scales, referral to specialist perinatal services and medication cautions, using NICE CG192.
findings: Every dose, threshold and timing was checked against the cited source section on 2026-10-18.
Normal values are typical adult reference ranges; laboratories differ.
unverifiedSections: The final 14,035 characters of the CG192 page were not read; postnatal screening timing (for example 4 to 6 weeks and 3 to 4 months) is not stated in the part read.
Scale cut-off scores for the Edinburgh Postnatal Depression Scale (EPDS) and Patient Health Questionnaire-9 (PHQ-9) were not given in the extract opened.
NICE CG192 gives no medication doses; no dosing source was opened.
No Saudi perinatal mental health guideline or Arabic validated scale cut-off was opened. No Saudi Ministry of Health or Saudi Society of Obstetrics and Gynaecology guideline was opened.
The Saudi Food and Drug Authority (SFDA) drug registration site could not be opened from this environment, so registration of each medicine was not verified; check hospital formulary.
Source pages were read through automated page extraction rather than page-by-page in the original documents, so each figure should be spot-checked against the source during clinical review.

pathophysiology.summary: Perinatal mental illness can be missed unless asked about; NICE advises asking at the first contact or booking visit and in the early postnatal period. A past or current history of severe mental illness, or severe perinatal illness in a first-degree relative, changes the referral pathway. Postpartum psychosis presents suddenly and needs assessment within 4 hours of referral. Risk assessment covers self-harm, suicidal thoughts and risks to others including the baby.

clinicalManagement.title: Ask at booking and early postnatally
actions: Ask the depression question and the GAD-2 questions; ask about past and present severe mental illness and family history.

clinicalManagement.title: Use scales for positive responses
actions: Use EPDS or PHQ-9 for depression and GAD-7 for anxiety; plan monitoring with validated questionnaires.

clinicalManagement.title: Refer by severity
actions: Severe illness suspected or any history: specialist perinatal mental health service.
Sudden-onset symptoms suggesting postpartum psychosis: immediate assessment within 4 hours of referral.

clinicalManagement.title: Stepped care
actions: Facilitated self-help for mild disease; high-intensity psychological intervention such as cognitive behavioural therapy for moderate or severe depression.

clinicalManagement.title: Medication cautions
actions: Do not offer valproate or carbamazepine for mental health problems in women planning pregnancy, pregnant or considering breastfeeding.
Do not offer lithium unless antipsychotics have not been effective; if continued, check levels every 4 weeks, then weekly from 36 weeks.

medicationPlan.note: NICE CG192 sets no doses. Do not offer valproate or carbamazepine in women planning pregnancy, pregnant or considering breastfeeding; do not offer lithium unless antipsychotics have not been effective, with lithium levels every 4 weeks and weekly from 36 weeks; use the lowest effective dose of antidepressants and consider discontinuation symptoms and neonatal adaptation syndrome, in particular with paroxetine and venlafaxine. Drug and dose choice belong to the perinatal psychiatrist. The Saudi Food and Drug Authority (SFDA) drug registration site could not be opened from this environment, so registration of each medicine was not verified; check hospital formulary.

diagnosticCriteria.criterion: GAD-2 (Generalised Anxiety Disorder two-item) score of 3 or more

diagnosticCriteria.threshold: Consider the EPDS or PHQ-9, or refer to the GP or mental health professional if severe illness is suspected.
Assess for treatment within 2 weeks of referral and provide psychological interventions within 1 month of initial assessment.
